recipes.name: Slow Cooker Northern White Bean Bacon Chowder
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups dried great Northern beans, rinsed

steps.text: Place beans in a large bowl with the water, cover, and soak overnight.
In a large skillet over medium to medium high heat, fry the bacon until crispy. Drain the bacon fat and crumble the bacon; set aside.
In a slow cooker, combine the carrot, celery, onion, potato, Italian- style seasoning, ground black pepper, reserved beans and crumbled bacon. Pour the broth over all.
Cover and cook on low setting for 7 1/2 to 9 hours, or until beans are crisp to tender.
Transfer 2 cups at a time to a blender or food processor and puree until smooth. Return all to slow cooker, add the milk, cover and heat on high for about 10 to 15 minutes, or until heated through.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Northern White Bean Bacon Chowder
raw_recipe.description: White beans which have been cooked in a slow cooker with bacon, aromatic vegetables, seasonings and chicken broth are pureed in a blender and thinned with milk in this recipe for a savory chowder.

review.reviewBody: This turned out really good tonight. I left out the italian seasoning, carrots, and celery. We added lots of garlic and it really added a nice flavor to it. I also didn't puree this at all. I cooked everything in the crockpot and added the milk during the last 30 minutes.

This was yummy! I used a pound of beans so I doubled the veggies except for the potato. Skipped the Italian seasoning and used a Cajun blend instead. When it was done cooking I pureed it in the pot using an immersion blender. I didn't measure the milk just poured it in until it was the consistency I wanted. It tasted a little flat at first so I added a few dashes of tobasco sauce, still wasn't right. Ended up adding 2 T of chopped cilantro to brighten it up. Then it was really good! Thanks for the recipe!

Great and easy recipe! I would definitely make this soup again for ease of prep and amazing flavor. The most time-consuming part of the prep was cooking the bacon; the rest was just quick chopping and dropping into the crock pot. 

I followed recipe as best I could. For the beans, I did the quick-soak method which worked just fine. I swapped an apple for the carrot out of necessity, but it was blended in the end and added a nice balance to the flavor. I used a stick blender and blended the soup about 85%, to preserve some texture from the veg and beans. 

I inadvertently added shredded cheese to the soup at the end, which was a happy accident! The bacon, potatoes, and cheese, when combined with the mild flavor of the white beans, made this soup taste like a loaded baked potato. So for a garnish, I used some reserved bacon crumbles and green onions to really ramp up the flavor. YUM-O!! Reheat Note: you may decide to add some water to thin the consistency just a bit; otherwise, it is super hearty and thick (which is still really good!).

 I HIGHLY recommend it to any first-time bean cookers and to anyone in the mood for a hearty and delicious wintertime soup.

One of my husband's favorite soups is bean with bacon. He liked this chowder, as did I. I used 3 cans(14.5 oz) of white northern beans instead of dried . I used 1 quart of chicken stock and kept the rest of the ingredients the same. I cooked it on low for a shorter time....6 hours. I used my immersion blender and did not use any dairy. This chowder is flavorful and filling.

This is a great soup. I alter the directions a bit to make it quicker. First I pressure cook the beans. It only takes a few minutes. Just put the beans in clear water and pressure cook for 20 minutes. (No salt in the water). Sautee the onions and celery a bit, then put everything together. I simmer for about 1 hour, no blender, also whipping cream or at least half and half. We all like the bits and pieces In the soup. I also do not use the Italian seasoning. just Basil and Oregano. A little different but the end result is still a great flavor.

great soup. i did cook the beans a little before adding them to the slow cooker cause the first time i made it i couldn't get the beans to cook. also, i put in a couple dried chipotle peppers when soaking the beans and threw them right into the mix. added an awesome smokey/spicey flavor. have tried it with different smoked meats, all turned out great. don't puree all of the soup, but do about half. saves the "refried beans" texture but is also not watery

I grew up eating lots of northern white bean on cornbread...so this is 
old-school comfort food for me. I didn't make cornbread to go with it, however, but did as another reviewer suggested and made garlic cheese toast to eat with it....yum. I do believe that it needs more flavor than what the bacon can give, so I stirred in 2 tablespoons of the bacon grease and I added abut 1/2 a cup of diced up leftover Christmas ham. I also followed the advice of others and didn't bother with any pureeing. Will make again!

Needs more liquid, I added additional chicken broth. Quite bland though, I would recommend more garlic or other seasoning depending on taste. Also I used an immersion hand blender, far easier than transferring to an upright blender.

The 5 stars are for the taste alone - it was wonderful!! However mine was not close to being thick enough to be a chowder. Most likely it's because I used 3 cans of beans & not dry (would have liked to use 4 but no more room in pot). 1/2# bacon w/all grease & added veg.'s to fry pan (after 2 min. in microwave) before adding to beans in slo-cooker. Only real change to recipe was I added 2 rounded tsp. of ham base. I over used stick blender & will have to be careful next time. I love bean soup & only remember 1 from the past that was better than this. This is GREAT!

Love this!I didn't have carrots that was the only thing missing and at the end it was very thick so i just added more chicken broth then milk.And i used my hand blender right in the crock pot to puree it.
Great soup recipe. I added a couple tsp. of liquid smoke to it while it cooked and it gave it a smokey meat flavor!

This was absolutely wonderful. I had a big jar of beans that I used to speed up the process but it was just fantastic soup. I actually forgot to save the recipe and I just found it again so I could make another batch! Highly recommended.
I made as written and made no changes. Served with jalapeno cornbread. Very filling and yummy :-)
This was really bland.
We enjoyed this recipe exactly as posted. It was a little bland so I added a little more sea salt and white pepper. We will be making this one again.
Incredibly easy to prepare and absolutely delicious! A big hit!

Tasted good the flaver was great,but i didn't quiet enjoy the texture it was like refried bean or baby food.I will make it again only puree half of the soup. I think it will give it the texture that me and my family will enjoy.

I was really excited about this recipe, but the flavor in this dish was really disappointing. It simply lacked completely in flavor. I tried it both pureed and not pureed as some other reviews suggested, but either way, it was just plain "blah". My husband and I both ate it (topped with shredded cheese, to try and "help" the flavor), but, unfortunately, I won't be making it again. I do alot of experimenting with recipes, but I made this according to the directions, and am not really sure what I could've added to make it better. Too bad.
was not impressed with this one. Flavor was OK but I would not blend any of it. Didn't like the texture. It would have probably been better with the beans whole. I will not use this recipe again.

I followed this recipe to the letter but left out the milk in the final step. After pureeing the whole batch, it was not nearly as thick as I would have liked and I did not want to water it down more by adding milk. To me, a bean chowder should be very thick and this was not. I would make this again but reduce the amount of broth called for.
